description:

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

In addition to being trespassed from the property, this suspect, Haley, was charged with prohibited possession of a weapon other than a firearm, which was discovered in her purse, disorderly conduct, obstructing, and resisting. She pleaded no contest to the charges of prohibited possession of a weapon other than a firearm and resisting, while the disorderly conduct and obstructing charges were dismissed. She was ultimately sentenced to 15 days in jail and 350 days of probation. Her shirt said, chase your dreams, not approval. Nice slogan until she started chasing her pride, which turned into catching a charge. I've seen this many times on the street, but I don't think someone wakes up thinking, you know what, today I'm going to fulfill my lifelong dream of getting arrested and riding in the back of a police car. It starts small, right, a request, a simple out, a person can walk away with their dignity attack, but ego, ego has to win. You can hear it in a voice, not fear, not confusion, commitment to being right and commitment to not backing down. Every time the officer gives her another chance, she doesn't see an opportunity, she sees a challenge. That's the trap, though, because some people would rather win an argument than win their freedom. And once pride grabs the will in these situations, logic gets thrown out the window. Now it's not about leaving anymore. It's about proving something to the cops, the strangers, to herself. This is how minor disagreements turning to handcuffs paperwork and a record that lasts way longer than the actual moment had to. That's life, though, because big consequences don't always come from big crime. Sometimes it comes from small moments where we just refuse to realize we're not the ones in control.
